clue.text: Outlaw's cover

definitions.meaning: short for hoodlum, a gangster or criminal
a covering for the head, or a car's bonnet

explanation.definitionFit: Hoodlum shortens to a word for a gangster, and the same word names a protective head covering.

clue.text: Unfairly treated boy had nerd being nasty

indicators.note: nasty suggests these letters are mangled into a different order

explanation.surface: A boy is picked on by a spiteful nerd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being nasty' is the anagram signal: BOYHADNERD rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for someone who has been treated unjustly and feels wronged.

clue.text: Sign either side of a river ultimately deters those on it?

indicators.note: the word for sign is split to sit on both sides of the other pieces

parts.note: an omen is a sign or portent

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of deters

explanation.surface: A warning sign on both banks of a river keeps people away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'either side of' puts O...MEN round A, R and S. 'those on it?' refers back to the river: rowers are on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowers sit on the water in boats, so they are the people found on a river.

clue.text: Condensed English is written by editor — very good man brought in

indicators.note: the phrase says one group of pieces is placed inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for very good
Tom is a man's name, and a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: An English text is written by an editor, with a saintly man included.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought in' places the very good man just after the opening E. PI as 'very good' (from pious) is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: To epitomise something is to sum it up in brief, so it is a synonym of condensed.

clue.text: Man leading disturbance — in charge of flag-waving?

indicators.note: leading puts the man's name in front of the next piece

parts.note: Pat is a man's name
a riot is a public disturbance

explanation.surface: A man heading a riot is in charge of the jingoistic flag-waving.
explanation.definitionFit: Waving flags is an outward show of love for one's country, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Top decoration from army, one a king received

indicators.note: received means the army's letters take in the others

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
I is the Roman numeral for one
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: An army gives a medal to one king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'received' puts I, A and R inside TA.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewelled headband is a decoration worn on top of the head, so a cryptic way to describe it.

clue.text: Drunken male rendering composition by German

indicators.note: drunken suggests the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A tipsy man sings a piece by a German composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunken' is the anagram signal for MALE RENDERING. Edward German was an English composer whose comic opera this is; the surface wants a composer from Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: This comic opera was written by the English composer Edward German, so it is a work by him.

clue.text: Court case involving food component

indicators.note: involving means the court case wraps round the food

parts.note: a suit is a lawsuit, a case in court
a bun is a small cake or bread roll

explanation.surface: A lawsuit is brought over an ingredient in food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court case' looks like a whole idea but is one word, a lawsuit; 'involving' signals the wrap-round.
explanation.definitionFit: A subunit is one constituent part of a larger whole, a synonym of component.

clue.text: Get a diary set up in which this can be fixed

indicators.note: set up says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the wanted letters sit inside the words Get a diary

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Buy a diary to arrange appointments in.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'in' as a link, but it signals the hidden run. In a down clue 'set up' means read upwards: ETAD turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: An appointment's day is what gets fixed in a diary, so the clue describes it.

clue.text: Unusual coin in dish.

parts.note: rare means unusual
a bit is an old small coin, as in a threepenny bit

explanation.surface: A rare coin is found in a serving dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Welsh rarebit is cheese on toast, a British dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit, melted cheese on toast, is a savoury dish.

clue.text: Message-bearer out of breath — he gulps awkwardly

indicators.note: awkwardly signals the letters are jumbled clumsily

explanation.surface: A messenger arrives out of breath, gulping clumsily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkwardly' is the anagram signal for BREATH HE GULPS.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal network that spreads rumour and news by word of mouth carries messages.

clue.text: An East European introducing British entertainer

parts.note: an gives A

indicators.note: introducing means one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: a Croat is a person from Croatia

explanation.surface: A man from Eastern Europe introduces a British performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introducing' puts B inside A + CROAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus tumbler is one kind of entertainer.

clue.text: What could make wild cat one so timid?

definitions.text: What could make wild cat one so timid?

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters run untamed into a fresh order

explanation.surface: What process could turn a wild cat into such a timid animal?
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' is the anagram signal for CAT ONE SO TIMID, and the whole clue also describes taming an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Taming is the process that turns a wild animal into a docile pet, as the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Country route? Train takes this for the match, they say

indicators.note: they say signals that the words are spoken, so a sound-alike is wanted

parts.words: Train takes this for the match
parts.note: a bride's train goes along the aisle to the wedding, a path for a bride

explanation.surface: A rail traveller asks which line goes to the football match.
explanation.walkthrough: Train is a wedding dress's trailing train, and the match is a marriage, not a game; the route sounds like a riding track.
explanation.definitionFit: A track for horse riders across the countryside is a rural route.

clue.text: Music group projecting end of piece the wrong way

indicators.note: the wrong way says the carpentry word is read backwards

parts.note: a tenon is the jutting end of a piece of wood that fits a mortise

explanation.surface: A band plays the final bit of a piece backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way' reverses TENON. 'piece' looks musical but is a piece of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is an ensemble of nine musicians.

clue.text: One causes pain, getting fellows stuck between a rock and a hard place

indicators.note: stuck between places the fellows in the middle of the two other pieces

parts.note: a tor is a rocky outcrop on a hill
another tor, a stony hilltop, read as a hard place
men means fellows

explanation.surface: Someone who inflicts suffering traps men in a desperate dilemma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuck between' puts MEN between two TORs; the idiom 'between a rock and a hard place' is read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A tormentor is a person who inflicts suffering on others.

clue.text: Deciding what correctly completed puzzle doesn't need

definitions.meaning: settling or making up one's mind

definitions.text: what correctly completed puzzle doesn't need
definitions.meaning: a puzzle already done right needs no second attempt at working it out

explanation.definitionFit: Resolving means deciding, and split as re-solving it means working a puzzle out again.

clue.text: Churches with foundation not entirely built around sand

indicators.note: built around means the shortened word is set round the other piece
not entirely means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the base is a foundation
silica is the mineral that makes up most sand

explanation.surface: Churches are built on foundations that are partly sand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' drops the final E, and 'built around' then sets the sand inside, between A and S.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica is a large oblong church, often granted special privileges by the Pope.

clue.text: Method of decorating stone needs sketch, first off

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight

indicators.note: first off removes the first letter of the word for sketch

parts.note: to pencil is to sketch

explanation.surface: Decorating stone requires a preliminary sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first off' takes P from PENCIL, leaving ENCIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A stencil is a cut-out template used to paint patterns, a way of decorating.

clue.text: Consented to abandon a sin

indicators.note: to abandon means the word drops the letter named next

parts.note: agreed means consented

explanation.surface: Someone agreed to give up wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to abandon' removes the A of AGREED.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: Account for discarded lover? Not good-looking!

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
plain means unattractive

explanation.surface: Someone asks why an unattractive former lover was dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To account for something is to give the reasons, a synonym.

clue.text: US writer who could make one dollar a page, having nothing to lose

indicators.note: could make suggests the letters are rearranged into a new name

parts.note: O is the round figure for nothing

explanation.surface: An American author might earn a dollar per page, with nothing to lose.
explanation.walkthrough: Take ONE DOLLAR A PAGE, remove O ('having nothing to lose'), and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of The Raven was an American writer of poems and tales.

clue.text: Technique using beam that reflects without distortion

indicators.note: the word mirrors itself exactly, reading the same in both directions

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A method uses a beam that bounces back unchanged.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a palindrome; 'reflects' also describes how the beam bounces back.
explanation.definitionFit: Radar locates objects by sending out radio waves and reading the echoes.

clue.text: This girl's turned up in a bar

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a rod is a bar

explanation.surface: A girl turns up in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses A + ROD; the bar is a rod, not a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Dora is a girl's given name, as in Dickens's Dora Spenlow, so 'this girl' points to it.

clue.text: One may grow fruit or vegetable crop

parts.note: chard is a leafy vegetable grown as a crop

explanation.surface: A grower chooses fruit or a vegetable crop.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit trees are grown in an orchard, so it is a place that grows fruit.

clue.text: Female initially elected for American state

indicators.note: initially puts the word for elected first

parts.note: a party voted into power is in
Diana is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman is the first elected for a US state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' is a position signal, not a first-letter pick: the elected word comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is one of the states of the USA.

clue.text: Fully aware about silver being ultra-fashionable

indicators.note: about means the first phrase goes round the second

parts.note: all there means mentally alert
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Someone sharp and wearing silver is very trendy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts AG inside ALL THERE.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for something very popular and in vogue at the moment.

clue.text: Short distance from island

definitions.meaning: a small unit of length, a twelfth of a foot
in Scotland a small island is called an ..., as in Inchcolm

explanation.definitionFit: A small length unit, and a Scottish word for a small island.
